136590.etyen:
From the female given name Guri, used as a euphemistic substitute for Gud (“God”).
The name continues Old Norse Guðríðr, traditionally explained as a contraction of Guðfríðr, containing guð (“god”) and Old Norse fríðr (“beautiful”). The interpretation of the first element is disputed; a connection with gunnr (“battle”) has also been proposed. The second element continues Proto-Germanic *frīdaz (“beautiful, beloved”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *preyH- (“to love”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk guri (“gosh, goodness”).

1000078.etyen:
Internationalism, based on English Namibia, coined in 1959 by the Namibian nationalist Mburumba Kerina from English Namib (“Namib Desert”) and New Latin -ia (“country-name-forming suffix”). The name refers to the Namib Desert, whose name is from Khoekhoe namib (“walkabout; wasteland”), from Khoekhoe nami (“to walk about”). The Khoekhoe name has consequently also been interpreted as referring to an empty or desolate area.
The territory had previously been known internationally as South West Africa. The name Namibia was adopted by the United Nations in 1968, before the country became independent
